title: C++ Exercises
description: Try a small question or coding task. The answer notes explain each step. Use the setup lesson to run these programs on your computer.

exercises.question: What does a C++ compiler do?
exercises.explanation: You write the source code. The compiler translates it and reports many mistakes before the program runs.
options: Turns source code into a program
Changes the colour of the screen
Stores every program on the web

exercises.question: Fill the gap: g++ ___ hello.cpp -o hello selects the C++20 rules.
exercises.explanation: The -std flag chooses the language version. These examples use C++20.

exercises.question: Why does this line fail to compile?
exercises.explanation: Braces stop this change because 3.5 would lose its .5 part. Use double when you need a decimal.
options: An int cannot keep the fractional part

exercises.question: What type does auto name = "Asha"; choose?
exercises.explanation: A text literal becomes a pointer to constant characters here. Use std::string name = "Asha"; for a string object.

exercises.question: Which word usually stops a switch case from continuing into the next case? ___
exercises.explanation: break leaves the switch. Without it, the next case can run too.

exercises.question: Print 1 to 15. Replace multiples of 3 with Fizz, 5 with Buzz, and both with FizzBuzz.
exercises.explanation: Checking both first matters. Otherwise 15 would match the 3 rule and print only Fizz.
checklist: Check multiples of both numbers first.

exercises.question: Which pair can be two overloads of add?
exercises.explanation: An overload is another function with the same name but different input types or input counts.
options: Two functions with the same inputs and only different return types

exercises.question: Write swapValues so it swaps the caller values. Use int& inputs.
exercises.explanation: A reference is another name for the same value. Changing a and b changes x and y.
checklist: Use references so the caller values change.

exercises.question: What does int value() const promise?
exercises.explanation: The const after the method inputs says it can read the object without changing its ordinary fields.
options: This method will not change ordinary fields of the object

exercises.question: Make a Counter class with add() and value(). It starts at zero and add() adds one.
exercises.explanation: The object remembers its count. Its public methods let other code add to it or read it.
checklist: Keep the count inside the object.
Print 1 after one call to add.

exercises.question: What does override help C++ check?
exercises.explanation: override catches mistakes such as spelling a method name wrong. The child must match a virtual method from the parent.
options: That every object has the same name
That a child method matches a virtual parent method

exercises.question: Fill the gap: ___ <typename T> starts a function recipe for different types.
exercises.explanation: A template leaves a place for a type. C++ fills in that place when the recipe is used.

exercises.question: How many items does this vector have?
exercises.explanation: The vector starts with two items. push_back adds one more at the end.

exercises.question: Which lambda is true when a number is greater than five?
exercises.explanation: The > sign means greater than. For example, 8 > 5 is true.

exercises.question: You should call delete yourself on the object owned by a unique_ptr.
exercises.explanation: The unique_ptr cleans up the object it owns. Deleting that object yourself can cause a second, invalid delete.

exercises.question: What does std::string("Hi, ") + "Asha" make?
exercises.explanation: The + sign joins the pieces of text. The first piece already contains the comma and space.
options: HiAsha with no space or comma

exercises.question: Fill the gap: score.___(0) reads an optional score or uses 0 if it is empty.
exercises.explanation: value_or uses the stored value when present. Otherwise it returns the fallback you supplied.
